modules.title: 支付回调重复送达时，怎样只生效一次？
这个案例怎样从失败变成可验收结果

items.title: 从重复处理改为原子领取
items.text: 支付平台可能并发发送事件 evt_7f2；服务端要用事件编号识别同一个业务动作，并通过唯一约束或等效操作原子取得处理权。其他请求只读取处理中或已保存结果，不再次创建订单或扣款。

items.title: 怎样观察改善
items.text: 首次和重复回调都应得到明确结果，调用方才能停止重试。让同一事件并发到达后，仍应只有一张订单、一次支付状态变化和对应的追踪记录。

items.title: 另一个场景：重复提交表单
items.text: 用户在网络卡顿时多次点击“创建项目”，客户端可为这次创建动作提供同一个幂等键；服务端原子领取该键并复用首次结果，避免生成多个项目。

modules.title: 仍不保证什么
modules.text: 幂等性约束的是同一个请求的预期业务效果；先查询再写入并不能抵挡并发重复请求，处理权必须原子取得。系统仍可能留下日志、审计记录或通知等副作用，外部服务的重复效果也需要它自身的幂等保护。

lessonPractice.title: 同一个支付回调因为超时被发送两次。哪种处理最合适？

options.label: 用稳定事件编号和唯一约束原子地取得处理权，其他请求复用已有结果
options.feedback: 对。稳定编号识别同一个业务动作，原子领取避免两个并发请求都开始处理，保存结果还能让重试得到一致反馈。

options.label: 让接口尽量快速返回，并要求支付平台不要再次重试
options.feedback: 你不能控制网络丢包和平台重试；没有服务端去重时，重复回调仍可能重复改变订单。

options.label: 只按到达时间判断新旧，把较晚的回调当成新订单处理
options.feedback: 到达时间不是业务身份，重复回调可能在不同时间到达，仍会被错误处理两次。

en.title: The same payment callback is sent twice after a timeout. Which handling is appropriate?

options.label: Use a stable event id and unique constraint to claim processing atomically; reuse the result for repeats
options.feedback: Correct. The stable id identifies one business action, the atomic claim prevents two concurrent handlers from starting it, and the saved result gives retries a consistent response.

options.label: Return as fast as possible and ask the payment provider never to retry
options.feedback: You cannot control packet loss or provider retries; without server-side deduplication, the order can still change twice.

options.label: Accept only by arrival time and treat a later callback as a new order
options.feedback: Arrival time is not business identity; the same callback can arrive later and still be processed twice.

lessonAgentPrompt.title: 你可以这样告诉 AI Agent
lessonAgentPrompt.text: 请让支付回调具备幂等性：以支付平台提供的稳定事件编号作为唯一键，用唯一约束或等效的原子操作在业务效果发生前取得处理权；重复回调返回已处理或处理中结果，不重复创建订单或扣款。让同一回调并发到达至少两次，确认只有一个请求取得处理权、只有一次业务状态变化。外部扣款也要使用同一幂等键或等效保护。

en.title: You can say this to an AI Agent
en.text: Make the payment callback idempotent: use the provider's stable event id as a unique key and claim processing with a unique constraint or equivalent atomic operation before the business effect. Return an already-processing or saved result for repeats without creating or charging twice. Deliver the same callback concurrently at least twice and verify that one request gains ownership and only one business state change occurs. Protect the external charge with the same idempotency key or an equivalent mechanism.

learning.assumes: You know that network requests can arrive again after a timeout or retry.
learning.outcome: You can choose a stable request identifier and verify that only one concurrent delivery claims processing and applies the business effect.

modules.title: How should a payment callback take effect only once when delivered twice?
How the case moves from failure to a verifiable result

items.title: Replace duplicate handling with an atomic claim
items.text: The provider may deliver event evt_7f2 concurrently. The server identifies one business action by its event id and uses a unique constraint or equivalent operation to claim processing atomically. Other requests only read the in-progress or saved result without creating or charging again.

items.title: How to observe the improvement
items.text: Give both first and repeated callbacks a clear result so the caller can stop retrying. After delivering the event concurrently, verify that there is still one order, one payment state change, and a matching trace record.

items.title: Another case: repeated form submission
items.text: When a slow network makes someone click Create project several times, the client can reuse one idempotency key for that creation. The server atomically claims the key and reuses the first result instead of creating multiple projects.

modules.title: What this still does not guarantee
modules.text: Idempotency constrains the intended business effect of the same request. A read-then-write check does not stop concurrent duplicates, so processing ownership must be claimed atomically. Logs, audit records, and notifications may still be side effects, and external services need their own idempotency protection.

distinctions.label: Side Effect
distinctions.text: {c:side-effect} describes external state changes caused by an operation; {c:idempotency} guarantees identical outcomes when repeated requests produce side effects only once.
